He directs an interdisciplinary team studying how conservation practices affect soil and water quality, owns the hydrology and water-quality side of that work, coordinates CEAP field efforts nationally, and leads the Eastern Corn Belt LTAR site. PhD, civil engineering, Texas A&M.

updates.name: Kimberly A. Novick
updates.bio: Environmental scientist and professor holding the Paul H. O'Neill Chair at Indiana University's O'Neill School, on the faculty since 2012. She studies land-atmosphere exchange of carbon, water and energy, especially drought and land-cover effects in eastern U.S. forests and farms, drawing on AmeriFlux, FLUXNET, NEON and satellite data, and serves on advisory councils for those networks.
updates.research_interests: land-atmosphere interactions; terrestrial carbon cycling; plant ecophysiology; nature-based climate solutions; drought impacts on forests and farms of the eastern United States; flux network synthesis (AmeriFlux, FLUXNET, NEON)

updates.name: Knute Nadelhoffer
updates.bio: Professor emeritus of ecology and evolutionary biology at the University of Michigan, where he directed the University of Michigan Biological Station from 2003 to 2020. Earlier he was an NSF ecosystem studies program director and a scientist at the Marine Biological Laboratory Ecosystems Center. His work covers forest soil carbon, nitrogen deposition and long-term detrital manipulation experiments.
